newsitem.title: USA: IBM reports Q2 after market close Monday.
newsitem.headline: IBM reports Q2 after market close Monday.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp will report second quarter earnings after the close of the U.S. stock market Monday, and earnings are expected to be on track, or slightly above the consensus.
Traders said that IBM's stock was volatile Monday because investors are nonetheless jittery, especially after Microsoft Corp just barely beat Wall Street's expectations.

"Everybody expects a good number, but people are afraid to say it because of Microsoft and the 'whisper' numbers," one technology trader said. According to First Call, the consensus estimate for IBM is $1.42 with a range from $1.36 to $1.50.

Traders and analysts said there were no "whisper" numbers circulating on IBM. Whisper numbers refer to earnings estimates that are either higher or lower than published Wall Street forecasts, which begin circulating the day or two before earnings are expected.
IBM's shares were volatile on Monday, after earlier jumping to a new high of $106-5/16 in intrasession trading, but falling back by midday to 103-7/8, off 5/8.
The day before Microsoft reported its fourth quarter earnings last week, its stock surged 9-31/32 as whisper numbers circulated on Wall Street.
"I think they will do better than consensus, but I don't think they will do $1.50," said Gary Helmig, a SoundView Financial analyst.
Helmig said that if IBM's earnings start becoming more consistent and predictable, investors will reward the computer giant with a better price/earnings ratio going forward.
Andrew Neff, a Bear Stearns analyst, said in a note that IBM's conference call could lead to a boost in its multiple.
Some analysts are looking for IBM to report an upside surprise. For example, John Jones, a Salomon Brothers analyst, said IBM could beat his estimate of $1.45 by five cents or so.
